title: Fourier analytic variants of the Furstenberg and Kakeya problems
summary: We study several distinct but related Fourier analytic variants of the well-known Kakeya and Furstenberg set problems in the plane. For example, given $0<s,t<1$, we call a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ an $(s,t)$-Kakeya set if there exists a set of directions $E \subseteq S^1$ with Hausdorff dimension at least $t$ such that, for each $e \in E$, the set $K$ contains a subset of a unit line segment in direction $e$ whose Fourier dimension, viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{R}$, is at least $s$.
